automation.starterPrompt: A managed environment moved. Each line of the event payload is one JSON event: `type` is what happened (`deploy_succeeded`, `deploy_failed`, `deploy_rolled_back`, `deploy_refused`, `stack_unhealthy`, `stack_recovered`, `secrets_changed`, `host_low_disk`, `host_low_memory`), `channelId` is `<repo>:<stack>` (or `device:<id>` for a server), `content` says it in a sentence and `extra` carries the facts: the deploy record's id, repository, stack, commit, computer, outcome and error. Read the stack with the deployments server's `environments` and `environment_history` tools, say what happened and what, if anything, the owner should do. Do not deploy, roll back or promote anything unless the user asks.

automationTemplates.title: Deployment alert
automationTemplates.prompt: Komodo just fired an alert, the payload is in $AUTOMATION_PAYLOAD: `level` is the severity, `target` names the resource ({type, id}), `data` carries the specifics, and `resolved` is true when this is the all-clear for an earlier alert. Use your Komodo capability to look up that resource and its recent container logs, then say what broke and what would fix it. Do not deploy, restart or stop anything unless the user asks.
automationTemplates.setup: In Komodo: Alerters → New Alerter → endpoint type Custom → paste this URL. Narrow it with the alerter's alert-type and resource filters.

automationTemplates.title: Investigate a failed deploy or an unhealthy stack
automationTemplates.note: only failed deploys, rollbacks and unhealthy stacks wake it
automationTemplates.prompt: A managed deploy failed or was rolled back, or a managed stack turned unhealthy on its computer. Each line of the event payload is one JSON event: `type` is `deploy_failed`, `deploy_rolled_back` or `stack_unhealthy` (any other line is another deploy event: leave it), `channelId` is `<repo>:<stack>`, and `extra` carries the record id, repo, stack, commit, device, outcome and error. For each of those events: read the stack with the deployments server's `environments` tool and its deploys with `environment_history` (the error, and the end of compose's output for a failed one), and read the containers' own logs on that computer with the devices tools (`run_command` there: `docker compose -p <stack> ps` and `docker compose -p <stack> logs --tail 200`). Then say what broke and what would fix it: a change in that repository at that commit (name the file and the cause), a secret or a grant the owner has to give, or something on the computer itself (a full disk, a port taken, a dependency down). Do not deploy, roll back, promote, restart or stop anything unless the user asks: a deploy that was rolled back already runs its last good version, and a fix goes through review before it ships.
automationTemplates.description: When a deploy of a stack your repositories declare fails or is rolled back, or the stack turns unhealthy, an agent reads its record and its logs and tells you what broke and what would fix it. It changes nothing by itself.

automationTemplates.title: Low disk or memory on a server
automationTemplates.note: only when a server runs short
automationTemplates.prompt: A computer this sandbox deploys stacks to is running short of disk or memory. Each line of the event payload is one JSON event: `type` is `host_low_disk` or `host_low_memory` (any other line is another deploy event: leave it), and `content` and `extra` say which computer and how much is left. Tell the owner in two or three lines: which computer, what is short, and by how much. If the devices tools reach that computer, add what is taking it, read-only (`docker system df`, `docker stats --no-stream`, `df -h`). Never prune, delete, stop or restart anything: what to free is the owner's call.
automationTemplates.description: Tells you when a computer your managed stacks run on runs short of disk or memory, and what is taking it. It changes nothing.
